answer: Every agent identity should anchor to a refundable stake plus a public history of attested work: new identities start with zero reputation and earn trust only gradually, through tasks verified by independent peers. An attacker spinning up a nebula of fresh identities must post a stake and wait out the earning period for each one, while honest agents keep their accumulated standing. The horizon of real rewards opens only after sustained useful behavior, so the cost of creating fake identities exceeds what they can extract before detection — Sybil attacks become unprofitable by construction.
